abstract: Newts regenerate their eye lens following its complete removal. To accomplish this, pigmented epithelial cells located in the dorsal iris transdifferentiate to lens epithelial cells. FGF and Wnt signaling pathways have been implicated during this process, but their association remained unclear. Here, we used FGF signaling inhibitors to stall lens regeneration and studied the affected downstream mechanisms using immunofluorescence, western blotting, and RNAseq. We showed that entry to the cell cycle was slowed, ERK levels were lower, and several genes were differentially regulated with FGF inhibition. Among the impacted genes were Wnt signaling modulators revealing a potential connection between the pathways. FGF inhibition also stalled the gradual increase in beta-catenin abundance in the nucleus and junctions in iris pigmented epithelial cells during lens regeneration. To place Wnt downstream of the FGF signaling pathway, we pharmacologically activated Wnt and showed that it is sufficient to rescue the lens regeneration stalling phenotype observed with FGF inhibition. Overall, our data indicate that FGF activates the Wnt signaling pathway during newt lens regeneration.
